n82dab0359a1.s: The Mandal Commission recommendations were implemented in 1990 by the government of:
n82dab0359a1.x: The V.P. Singh Government implemented the Mandal recommendations in 1990; 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved for OBCs from 1993.

nindian-society-42-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: It examined sub-categorisation within OBCs in the Central List
It examined sub-categorisation of Scheduled Tribes in the Central List
It aimed at equitable distribution of reservation benefits among under-represented groups
It submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023
nindian-society-42-3.x: The Rohini Commission examined sub-categorisation of OBCs, not Scheduled Tribes, in the Central List so that benefits reach under-represented groups.

n73087ce63c8.s: EWS reservation, which stands outside the 50 per cent ceiling on backward-class quotas, was provided under Articles:
n73087ce63c8.x: The 50 per cent ceiling applies to backward-class reservations; EWS reservation was added over and above it through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).

n0ae486d9c38.s: According to Indra Sawhney, carry-forward of unfilled reserved vacancies is:
o: Unlimited and calculated once in a decade
Allowed, within the 50 per cent ceiling applied year by year
n0ae486d9c38.x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.

nc20cd56454f.s: Which Constitutional Amendment restored the power of the States to identify and list SEBCs?
nc20cd56454f.x: The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the States' power to list SEBCs; the 102nd (2018) had given the NCBC constitutional status and inserted Article 342A.

nfba26cc79ca.s: In August 2026, after the Rohith Nathan verdict, the Centre sought clarification on how many CSE-2025 candidates?
nfba26cc79ca.x: Following the 11 March 2026 verdict that parental salary alone cannot decide creamy-layer status, the Centre sought clarification on 958 CSE-2025 candidates. (A sequence needs more dated events than the original gives, so a one-liner is used.)

n91e48801574.s: In admissions, EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment extends to:
n91e48801574.x: EWS reservation applies to Central educational institutions and posts and extends to private educational institutions; it is not mandatory for the States.

n8870eab6013.s: For EWS eligibility, the agricultural land held by the family must be below:
n8870eab6013.x: The EWS criteria are family income below Rs 8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 sq ft.

n4cbae16ab67.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the Supreme Court's triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies?
o: Prior approval of the quota by the National Commission for Backward Classes
A dedicated commission to examine backwardness
Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise
Keeping total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling
n4cbae16ab67.x: The triple test is a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportion and a total within 50 per cent; NCBC approval is not one of its parts.

nab05cadb089.s: The expression 'Backward Classes' in the Constitution is:
nab05cadb089.x: The Constitution does not define 'Backward Classes'; Article 340 only provides for a commission to investigate their conditions.

n3dc2ac7743f.s: In Article 342A, SEBC stands for Socially and ____ Backward Classes.
n3dc2ac7743f.x: SEBC means Socially and Educationally Backward Classes; 'Economically' is the usual distractor.

n513d260648d.s: NSTFDC lends to Scheduled Tribes with annual income up to:
n513d260648d.x: NSTFDC, set up in 2001, lends to STs with income up to double the poverty line, not three times.

n6fc7ae5f4ee.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, each Sub-Divisional and District Level Committee has how many members?
n6fc7ae5f4ee.x: The Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees are six-member bodies of revenue, tribal and forest officials and elected panchayat members.

nf8d9156816d.s: In relation to laws inconsistent with it, the Forest Rights Act, 2006:
o: Applies only where no State law exists
Can be overridden by an executive circular
nf8d9156816d.x: The Forest Rights Act overrides laws that are inconsistent with its provisions.

n3d54ed6a1fd.s: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs sought funds for managing Community Forest Resource areas vested in Gram Sabhas from the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
n3d54ed6a1fd.x: MoTA sought MoEFCC funds for managing CFR areas vested in Gram Sabhas; this is separate from the criticism of the Agasthyamalai evictions.

nindian-society-40-5.s: Besides forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes, the Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises the forest rights of:
nindian-society-40-5.x: The Act recognises individual and community forest rights of forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.

nindian-society-35-25.s: The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission is run by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with the Ministry of:
nindian-society-35-25.x: The Mission is run by Health and Family Welfare with Tribal Affairs and focuses on screening tribal populations.

nindian-society-37-12.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-AJAY?
o: Its portal supports planning and monitoring of works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams
It is targeted at Scheduled Castes
It is a portal for tribal artisans to sell forest produce
nindian-society-37-12.x: PM-AJAY plans, pools funds for and monitors works in SC-majority Adarsh Grams; the tribal artisans' marketplace is TRIFED/Tribes India.

nc791ade01c1.s: In scheduling a community as a Scheduled Tribe, the State's proposal is first examined by the:
nc791ade01c1.x: The sequence is State proposal, Registrar General of India, NCST, Union Cabinet, and amendment by Parliament under Article 342(2).

n067c587fd8f.s: The 1970 amendment to the AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation added:
o: Removal of the bar on land transfers to non-tribals
A presumption that land belongs to tribals and a bar on transfers even between non-tribals
Permission for transfers approved by a private company
Application of the Regulation only to urban municipal areas
n067c587fd8f.x: Regulation 1 of 1970 presumed Scheduled Area land to be tribal and barred transfers even between non-tribals.

n221c2723cb8.s: Since the State is barred from leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals, mining in AP Scheduled Areas is left to:
o: Private companies with Gram Sabha consent
Any company approved by the Centre
Non-tribal individuals holding up to 4 ha
n221c2723cb8.x: The State cannot lease Scheduled Area land to non-tribals, so mining is left to State undertakings or tribal cooperatives; Gram Sabha consent does not validate a private lease.

n55f1282f382.s: PM-JANMAN, launched in November 2023, covers how many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups?
n55f1282f382.x: PM-JANMAN was launched in November 2023 for the development of 75 PVTGs.

n81d1738fdbb.s: How many Ministries are involved in the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (September 2024)?
n81d1738fdbb.x: The Abhiyan involves 17 Ministries and covers about 63,000 tribal villages.

nindian-society-35-12.s: PM-JANMAN stands for PM Janjati Adivasi ____ Maha Abhiyan.
nindian-society-35-12.x: PM-JANMAN is the PM Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan for STs, especially PVTGs, with housing, roads, water and electricity.

nb6e72bc48ab.s: Scheduled Areas cover about what share of Andhra Pradesh?
nb6e72bc48ab.x: Scheduled Areas cover 10.15 per cent of AP; STs number 27.39 lakh, 5.53 per cent of the population.

nda57a2c8435.s: In PESA areas of Andhra Pradesh, at least what share of seats is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
nda57a2c8435.x: In PESA areas at least 50 per cent of seats go to STs and all chairpersons are STs.

na37fae793f4.s: Compared with the State average, tribal MMR and IMR in Andhra Pradesh are:
na37fae793f4.x: Both the tribal maternal mortality ratio and infant mortality rate are above the State average.

n87227a1d660.s: Article 51A(k), the parent's duty to educate a child aged 6-14, was added by which Amendment?
n87227a1d660.x: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A, rewrote Article 45 and added Article 51A(k).

n8e7abd63c3b.s: Survival, development, protection and ____ are the four broad categories of rights under the UNCRC.
n8e7abd63c3b.x: The four categories are survival, development, protection and participation; education is not a separate category.

n7e10f0f3354.s: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child contains how many articles?
n7e10f0f3354.x: The UNCRC (20 November 1989) has 54 articles; India acceded on 11 December 1992.

nefc564272cb.s: Which of the following lies outside the statutory entitlement of the RTE Act, 2009?
o: Neighbourhood schools for children aged 6 to 14
nefc564272cb.x: The RTE Act covers free and compulsory elementary education (6-14, Classes 1-8); pre-school and secondary education are not included.

n3270d8d5f93.s: At the national level, monitoring and grievance redressal under the RTE Act is done by the:
o: National Council of Educational Research and Training
National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
n3270d8d5f93.x: NCPCR and the State Commissions monitor and redress grievances under the RTE Act; SMCs are school-level bodies.

na9a83934072.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the RTE Act, 2009 is correctly matched?
na9a83934072.x: The RTE Act gives effect to Article 21A, covers children aged 6-14 (Classes 1-8) and came into force on 1 April 2010.

n513d9f9f814.s: Samagra Shiksha (2018) merged Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and:
n513d9f9f814.x: Samagra Shiksha merged SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education into one school education scheme.

na25664fd242.s: Besides the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 and the RTE Act, 2009, the NCPCR specifically monitors the:
na25664fd242.x: NCPCR monitors the JJ Act 2015, POCSO Act 2012 and RTE Act 2009, not the Child Labour Amendment Act 2016 or its own parent law.

n97fd3eb159d.s: Survival, health and nutrition; education and development; protection; and ____ are the four priority areas of the National Policy for Children, 2013.
n97fd3eb159d.x: The fourth priority area of NPC 2013 is participation; vocational employment is not one of them.

nindian-society-1-14.s: The first child labour law in India was the:
o: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
nindian-society-1-14.x: The 1933 Children (Pledging of Labour) Act was the first child labour law; the 1986 Act was the first comprehensive one.

new.s: Under Article 340, a commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes is appointed by the:
new.x: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission on socially and educationally backward classes; Kalelkar, Mandal and Rohini were set up under it.

new.s: For the Central Educational Institutions Act, OBCs are the classes 'so determined' by the:
new.x: Under the CEI (Reservation in Admission) Act, OBCs are the classes so determined by the Central Government.

new.s: Article 16(4B) provides for:
o: Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs
Carrying forward unfilled backlog vacancies as a separate class
10 per cent EWS reservation in posts
new.x: Article 16(4B), added by the 81st Amendment (2000), treats unfilled backlog vacancies as a separate class outside the 50 per cent ceiling.

new.s: Which of the following reservation provisions was part of the original Constitution?
new.x: Article 16(4) was in the original Constitution; 15(4) came by the 1st (1951), 16(4A) by the 77th and 15(5) by the 93rd Amendment.

new.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes is a constitutional body under Article:
new.x: The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B, giving the NCBC constitutional status; 338A is the NCST and 342A deals with SEBC lists.

new.s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment (2001) is associated with:
new.x: The 85th Amendment gave consequential seniority with promotion, nullifying the 'catch-up' rule; backlog carry-forward was the 81st and relaxed marks the 82nd.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about constitutional amendments on reservation:
1. The 82nd Amendment provided relaxed qualifying marks in promotion for SCs/STs.
2. The 89th Amendment inserted Article 16(4B) on backlog vacancies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only 1 is correct: the 82nd Amendment added the proviso to Article 335; the 89th split the SC/ST Commission, and 16(4B) came from the 81st.

new.s: The 105th Constitutional Amendment Act was introduced in Parliament as the:
new.x: The 105th Amendment was the 127th Bill; the 102nd was the 123rd Bill and the 103rd the 124th Bill.

new.s: The Mandal Commission (1979) was set up through which Ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
new.x: The Janata Government of Morarji Desai set up the Mandal Commission through the Ministry of Home Affairs; the Rohini Commission came through Social Justice and Empowerment.

new.s: How many backward castes were identified by the Kaka Kalelkar Commission?
new.x: The Kalelkar Commission listed 2,399 backward castes, 837 of them 'most backward'; 3,743 is the Mandal figure.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the B.P. Mandal Commission:
1. It used 11 indicators of backwardness.
2. It estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: the Mandal Commission used 11 social, educational and economic indicators and put the OBC share at 52 per cent.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Kaka Kalelkar Commission:
1. It was the first commission to use social and educational criteria for backwardness.
2. Its recommendations were implemented by the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only 1 is correct: the Kalelkar Commission first used social and educational criteria, but its report was not implemented and was rejected in 1961.

new.s: The Justice G. Rohini Commission submitted its report to the President on:
new.x: The Rohini Commission, set up in October 2017, reported on 31 July 2023; 30 March 1955 was the Kalelkar report.

new.s: Which case held that reservation should generally stay within 50 per cent and that caste is not the sole test?
o: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
new.x: M.R. Balaji (1962) laid down the 50 per cent limit and held caste is not the sole test of backwardness.

new.s: Which case upheld the 93rd Amendment and the 27 per cent OBC quota under the CEI Act?
new.x: Ashoka Kumar Thakur (2008) upheld the 93rd Amendment and the 27 per cent OBC quota, applying the creamy layer to OBCs but not SCs/STs.

new.s: In the Maratha reservation case (Jaishri Patil, 2021), the Supreme Court:
o: Upheld the Maratha quota as an extraordinary case
Struck down the Maratha SEBC quota as breaching the 50 per cent limit
new.x: Jaishri Patil (5 May 2021) struck down the Maratha quota, finding no extraordinary case beyond 50 per cent; its ruling on SEBC lists was reversed by the 105th Amendment.

new.s: Which of the following case–ruling pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jarnail Singh – creamy layer can apply to SC/ST promotions
M. Nagaraj – struck down the 77th Amendment
P.A. Inamdar – upheld quota in private unaided institutions
Champakam Dorairajan – upheld a caste-based quota
new.x: Jarnail Singh (2018) allowed the creamy layer in SC/ST promotions; Nagaraj upheld the 77th, Inamdar barred quota in private unaided institutions, and Champakam struck the quota down.

new.s: On which point did Indra Sawhney overrule M.R. Balaji?
o: Reservation must stay within 50 per cent
Caste can be the main criterion of backwardness
Creamy layer must be excluded from SCs
new.x: Indra Sawhney held caste can be the main criterion of backwardness, overruling Balaji on this; it kept the 50 per cent ceiling and denied promotion quota.

new.s: When the OBC creamy-layer income limit was first fixed in 1993, it was:
new.x: The limit was Rs 1 lakh in 1993, raised to Rs 2.5 lakh (2004), Rs 4.5 lakh (2008), Rs 6 lakh (2013) and Rs 8 lakh (2017).

new.s: In Janhit Abhiyan (2022), the Chief Justice who dissented on EWS reservation was:
new.x: The five-judge bench upheld EWS by 3:2; the dissenters were CJI U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat.

new.s: EWS reservation under the 103rd Amendment is meant for economically weaker sections:
o: Not covered by SC, ST or OBC quotas
Including OBCs above the creamy layer only
Within the existing SC and ST quotas
new.x: The 10 per cent EWS quota is for sections not covered by SC/ST/OBC quotas and is over and above existing reservation.

new.s: The 27 per cent OBC quota in Central Government jobs began in:
new.x: The Mandal recommendations were implemented in 1990, but the 27 per cent quota in central posts operated from 1993; the CEI Act seats came in 2007.

new.s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission?
new.x: The Anantharaman Commission (report 1970) was the first AP BC Commission; Muralidhara Rao took charge in 1982 and Manjunatha (2016) dealt with Kapus.

new.s: When N.T. Rama Rao introduced BC reservation in AP local bodies in 1984, the quota was:
new.x: NTR introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in 1984; it was later raised to 34 per cent and cut to 24.15 per cent under GOs 176, 559 and 560.

new.s: The Justice Manjunatha Commission (2016) proposed a 5 per cent quota for Kapus under which category?
new.x: The Manjunatha Commission led to a 2017 Bill giving Kapus 5 per cent as BC-F; it was never approved by the Centre.

new.s: The Lokur Committee (1965) is known for:
o: Laying down five criteria for identifying Scheduled Tribes
Studying the health and educational status of tribes in 2013
new.x: The Lokur Committee gave five ST criteria; Bhuria was the basis of PESA, Dhebar studied Scheduled Areas and Xaxa reported in 2013.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Lokur Committee criteria for Scheduled Tribes?
new.x: The five criteria are primitive traits, distinct culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact and backwardness; ST status is religiously neutral.

new.s: The Dhebar Commission (1960-61) on Scheduled Areas and ST welfare was set up under Article:
new.x: The U.N. Dhebar Commission was set up under Article 339; Article 340 is for backward classes and 342 for ST lists.

new.s: Which of the following committee–work pairs is correctly matched?
o: Lokur Committee – Article 339 Commission on Scheduled Areas
Xaxa Committee – five ST criteria of 1965
Dhebar Commission – 2013 study of tribal health and education
new.x: The Bhuria Committee formed the basis of PESA; Dhebar was the Article 339 Commission, Lokur gave the 1965 criteria and Xaxa did the 2013 study.

new.s: The High-Level Committee (2013) on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribes was headed by:
new.x: Virginius Xaxa headed the 2013 High-Level Committee; Dhebar headed the 1960-61 Commission and Bhuria the committee behind PESA.

new.s: In tribal usage, which of the following would be called a 'Diku'?
new.x: Diku means an outsider-exploiter such as a moneylender, trader, landlord or contractor.

new.s: The assimilation approach, which saw tribals as 'backward Hindus' to be absorbed, is associated with:
new.x: G.S. Ghurye (with N.K. Bose) argued assimilation; early Elwin argued isolation and Nehru integration.

new.s: The Santhal Hul (1855-56), directed against the dikus, was led by:
new.x: Sidhu and Kanhu led the Santhal Hul; Birsa led the Ulgulan, Alluri the Rampa rebellion and Vempatapu the Srikakulam movement.

new.s: Birsa Munda's Ulgulan led to the enactment of the:
o: AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation, 1959
new.x: The Ulgulan (1899-1900), aiming at Abua Raj, led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.

new.s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 came into force on:
new.x: The Act came into force on 31 December 2007 and its rules on 1 January 2008; 13 December 2005 is the cut-off date.

new.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, how many titles have been distributed in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP has distributed 2,26,651 titles covering 4,54,706 acres.

new.s: Under the Forest Rights Act, ownership of minor forest produce is a/an:
new.x: Ownership of minor forest produce, like nistar, grazing and CFR management, is a community right under FRA; bamboo counts as MFP.

new.s: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 exempts strategic projects located within what distance of the borders?
new.x: The 2023 Amendment exempts strategic projects within 100 km of the borders, a point in the tribal rights debate.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Forest Rights Act, 2006?
o: The Gram Sabha initiates determination of rights
Its nodal ministry is Tribal Affairs
It gives ownership of minerals to forest dwellers
The ceiling is 4 ha per family
new.x: The Act gives no ownership of minerals; the Gram Sabha initiates claims, Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry and the ceiling is 4 ha.

new.s: The PESA Act, 1996 extends Part IX of the Constitution to:
new.x: PESA extends the Panchayat provisions of Part IX to Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) areas.

new.s: Under the AP PESA Rules, 2011, how many PESA Gram Sabhas are there in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh has 2,038 PESA Gram Sabhas under its 2011 PESA Rules.

new.s: How many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups are there in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP has 12 PVTGs, including Chenchu, Bodo Gadaba, Konda Reddi and Kolam, out of 75 in India.

new.s: Which of the following is a PVTG of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Chenchu is among AP's 12 PVTGs; Bharia (MP) and Kamar and Baiga (Chhattisgarh) were the first PVTGs to get habitat rights.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for identifying a PVTG?
new.x: PVTG criteria are pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, economic backwardness and a stagnant or declining population.

new.s: The 75 PVTGs of India are spread over:
new.x: The 75 PVTGs live in 18 States and 1 UT.

new.s: The Tribal Sub-Plan is now called the:
new.x: The TSP is now the Development Action Plan for STs (DAPST); DAPSC is the renamed SC plan.

new.s: Which State law, of 2013, was the first to make SC and Tribal Sub-Plan allocation binding?
new.x: The AP Scheduled Castes Sub-Plan and Tribal Sub-Plan Act, 2013 was the first State law making the allocation binding.

new.s: TRIFED, which runs Tribes India and gives MSP for minor forest produce, was set up in:
new.x: TRIFED dates from 1987; NSFDC is 1989, NSKFDC 1997 and NSTFDC 2001.

new.s: How many Scheduled Tribe communities are notified in Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: AP has 34 ST communities with 27.39 lakh people; 12 of them are PVTGs.

new.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation of Andhra Pradesh was founded in:
new.x: The GCC (1956) buys MFP at fair prices, runs PDS depots and gives credit to tribal farmers.

new.s: Self-employment schemes and rehabilitation of Jogins in Andhra Pradesh are handled by the:
new.x: The AP SC Cooperative Finance Corporation handles self-employment and Jogin rehabilitation.

new.s: Which State has the most Eklavya Model Residential Schools?
new.x: Odisha has the most EMRS; the national target is 740 with 511 running (Aug 2026).

new.s: Stand-Up India loans for greenfield enterprises range from:
new.x: Stand-Up India (5 April 2016) gives Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore to SC/ST and women borrowers; Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 crore is the VCF-SC range.

new.s: The Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence were launched on 22 April 2022 at:
new.x: DACE gives Civil Services coaching in Central Universities and was launched at BHU.

new.s: How many National Overseas Scholarships are given each year for ST students?
new.x: There are 20 awards (17 ST and 3 PVTG) with a Rs 6 lakh income limit.

new.s: Special provisions for women and children are permitted under Article:
new.x: Article 15(3), in the original Constitution, allows special provisions for women and children.

new.s: Traffic in human beings and forced labour are prohibited by Article:
new.x: Article 23 bans traffic in human beings and forced labour; Article 24 bars children below 14 from factories and mines.

new.s: Which Article directs that the tender age of children is not abused and that they are not forced by economic necessity into unsuited avocations?
new.x: Article 39(e) protects the tender age of children; 39(f) concerns healthy development in freedom and dignity.

new.s: The Unni Krishnan case (1993) on the right to free education arose from which State?
new.x: Unni Krishnan v. State of AP arose from Andhra Pradesh and held children below 14 have a right to free education under Article 21.

new.s: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011) dealt with:
o: The 25 per cent quota in private schools
Child trafficking and children in circuses
The right to free education under Article 21
new.x: Bachpan Bachao Andolan dealt with child trafficking and children in circuses, with FIRs for missing children.

new.s: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, later merged into Samagra Shiksha, was launched in:
new.x: SSA began in 2001 and was merged into Samagra Shiksha in 2018; 1968 was the first NPE and 1975 the start of ICDS.

new.s: For North-Eastern and hill States, Samagra Shiksha funds are shared between the Centre and States in the ratio:
new.x: Samagra Shiksha is funded 60:40, and 90:10 for North-Eastern and hill States.

new.s: Universal Children's Day is observed on:
new.x: 20 November is Universal Children's Day and the UNCRC adoption date; 14 November is India's Children's Day.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Optional Protocols to the UNCRC:
1. India ratified the two 2000 Optional Protocols in 2005.
2. India is a party to the 2011 Protocol on a communications procedure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only 1 is correct: India ratified both 2000 Protocols in 2005 but is not a party to the 2011 communications procedure Protocol.

new.s: While inquiring into complaints, the NCPCR has the powers of a:
new.x: The NCPCR has civil-court powers while inquiring into complaints.

new.s: The POCSO Act, 2012 came into force on:
new.x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act came into force on 14 November 2012 and defines a child as below 18.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the POCSO Act, 2012?
o: It defines a child as a person below 18
Its 2019 Amendment provides death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault
It came into force on 14 November 2012
new.x: The 2019 Amendment, notified 16 August 2019, provides death penalty for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on children; POCSO is gender-neutral.

new.s: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance, April 2018 made death penalty possible for rape of a girl below:
new.x: The April 2018 Ordinance allowed death penalty for rape of a girl below 12.

new.s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, the preliminary assessment of a 16-18 year old accused of a heinous offence is made by the:
new.x: The Juvenile Justice Board makes the preliminary assessment; the case may then go to the Children's Court to be tried as an adult.

new.s: Under the JJ Act, 2015, children in need of care and protection are dealt with by the:
new.x: Child Welfare Committees handle children in need of care and protection; JJBs deal with children in conflict with law.

new.s: After the 2021 amendment to the JJ Act, adoption orders are issued by the:
new.x: The 2021 amendment, in force from 1 September 2022, empowers the District Magistrate to issue adoption orders.

new.s: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 does NOT apply to:
new.x: HAMA covers Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs; the JJ Act route is open to all religions.

new.s: Under the Adoption Regulations, 2022, a surrendered child's parents get a reconsideration period of:
new.x: The Adoption Regulations 2022 give a 2-month reconsideration period for a surrendered child.

new.s: India's first National Policy for Children was adopted in:
new.x: The first National Policy for Children was in 1974; NPC 2013 replaced it.

new.s: CHILDLINE 1098 has been integrated with which emergency response number?
new.x: CHILDLINE 1098 is integrated with ERSS-112 across 36 States/UTs.

new.s: TrackChild, which tracks missing and found children, works under:
new.x: TrackChild is a Women and Child Development portal under Mission Vatsalya.

new.s: Which of the following indicator–figure pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The overall sex ratio was 943 in Census 2011; 914 was the provisional child sex ratio and 1,020 the NFHS-5 figure.

new.s: As per Census 2011, the number of child main workers aged 5-14 was about:
new.x: Census 2011 counted 4.35 million child main workers; about 10.1 million including marginal workers.
